E1 vs H2a.reasons: Both documents would lead the committee to the same defensible decision with correct core numbers. X serves the CEO's four requests more completely. It gives the recommendation, a cash bridge with headroom even if the lease is triggered, a fuller gate set including process proof at full speed, and a five-layer contingency with costs, timings and owners. It also tests whether the lease's 1% edge survives volume, price, scrap and start-up timing. Both documents would lead the committee to the same defensible decision with correct normalised economics, a cash and capital test, and a delivery contingency. Y serves the decision maker better. E1 vs H2a.reasons: Both documents are defensible and meet all four of the key's criteria: margins reconciled to avoidable cash, the penalty treated as one-time, D substitution bounded by capacity and validation, and no causal reading of the renewal gap. Y serves the board better because it delivers more of what the committee asked for. It gives a time-phased comparison of exit, retain, delayed sunset and redesign against each constraint. It adds sensitivities showing the conclusion is robust: no migration rate makes exit pay, the redesign breaks even at 19–31% of the estimated saving, and exit needs a 70% fall in C contribution. It also provides a concrete contract plan, quantified gates and a transparent assumption log. X is accurate, leaner, and more disciplined about not quantifying the engineering opportunity cost. But it offers less decision support on downside cases, gate thresholds and the redeploy-to-D question.
